messages:
acme_ops: Hey @lisa_support — we've got a tough one. Since the 03/16 midnight rollout, our account is seeing inconsistent answers within the same user session. Two identical requests in the same session return different completions. High impact for our product.

lisa_support: Sorry for the trouble, @acme_ops. Can you paste a minimal repro (request body + response IDs)? Also, any request_ids / response_ids from logs will help.

acme_ops: Repro: we call conversation.create with session_token=st_abc123. Two sequential calls within 10s return different outputs. Example (redacted):
```
POST /v1/chat/completions
Authorization: Bearer sk-***
{
  "model": "redwood-chat-1",
  "session_token": "st_abc123",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"When does downtown store close today?"}],
  "max_tokens": 60
}
```
Responses we got (different completions, same session):
- response_id: r_11x, model_variant: redwood-chat-1@v2 -> "It closes at 9pm tonight."
- response_id: r_11y, model_variant: redwood-chat-1@v1-quant -> "It closes at 7pm tonight."

matt_cs: That looks like routing to two different model variants mid-session. Do you have request IDs / X-Request-ID headers? If you can share timestamps we can correlate with runtime logs.

acme_ops: We have request header x-request-id: req-ACME-98765 for r_11x (09:12:10 UTC) and req-ACME-98766 for r_11y (09:12:18 UTC). Both sent from same client socket, same session_token.

lisa_support: Thanks. I'm opening an eng investigation. @jordan_ml can you weigh in — this looks like a variant fallback / routing case.

jordan_ml: From initial glance: possible cause is the new canary swap for redwood-chat-1 that started rolling midnight UTC. If the routing policy is not sticky to session_token, requests can route to different compatible variants when autoscaler shifts capacity or a fallback triggers.

sam_sre: Logged the two request ids and traced them through the runtime. The first went to pool gpu-dedicated-42 -> variant_id v2. The second was routed to gpu-burst-7 -> variant_id v1-quant (fallback pool). I see a routing transition event at 09:12:15 UTC.

acme_ops: So how is it possible that the same session_token lost affinity? We are using long-lived session_token for affinity.

jordan_ml: Two possible bugs: 1) session affinity lookup key changed in the rollout (we started hashing on request_id in addition to session_token for sticky assignment); 2) fallback routing intentionally ignores affinity when capacity is low and does an unsticky variant assignment. Either will cause intra-session variant mixing.

lisa_support: Action items: (1) collect full request/response payloads and the associated runtime route logs (we have those for the two req IDs), (2) temporarily enable "variant_pin=true" for acme's account to force single variant while we investigate, (3) dev reproduce task. @deploy-bot please set a mitigation flag on tenant acme-42.

deploy-bot: mitigation flag set: tenant=acme-42, variant_pin=true (expires 2026-03-17T12:30:00Z) :white_check_mark:

matt_cs: @acme_ops — can you confirm whether you want variant_pin until we fix routing? Also, please confirm whether the discrepancy affects only content (fact mismatch) or also safety/formatting.

acme_ops: Confirm pin for now. It's a factual discrepancy that breaks our UI (users see conflicting facts in same session). We'll keep sampling and send any other examples.

jordan_ml: For the eng repro: steps we took
1) create session_token st_repro_001
2) send identical prompt twice in <30s
3) observe variant assignment via runtime log
We reproduced locally with a canary toggle and observed: when fallback to burst pool occurs mid-session, affinity was not preserved and the second request used quantized variant.

sam_sre: Logs (sanitized):
```
[09:12:09] req=req-ACME-98765 session=st_abc123 route=pool/gpu-dedicated-42 variant=redwood-chat-1@v2 token_hash=0x12af
[09:12:15] route-change event: pool/gpu-dedicated-42 scaled_down -> shortage_notify
[09:12:16] req=req-ACME-98766 session=st_abc123 route=pool/gpu-burst-7 variant=redwood-chat-1@v1-quant token_hash=null
```

jordan_ml: Note token_hash=null in second log — that's the smoking gun. The affinity lookup failed. Preliminary fix: ensure session_token is validated as the primary stickiness key and never null-out on fallback path. Also add a regression test to simulate mid-request pool drain.

lisa_support: ETA for a hotfix?

jordan_ml: We'll do a hotpatch to honor session_token for fallback routing. I can have a patch + canary roll within 4 hours. Full rollout after validation ~24h.

matt_cs: I'll keep acme_ops updated. For traceability, please attach the two runtime logs and the two API request bodies to this thread (or send them via secure upload).

acme_ops: Uploaded the full logs to the secure bucket (link redacted). Let us know when the hotfix is live so we can unpin.

lisa_support: Thanks all. Next steps: Jordan does hotfix canary -> Sam validates traces for a few samples -> Matt coordinates with ACME to unpin when safe. I'll keep this thread open and post status updates. :thumbsup:

jordan_ml: Pushing canary now. Will report when validation completes.

sam_sre: Validated 5 test requests from acme sample set after canary: all routed to pinned variant. No variant mixing observed in 10 warm-up runs.

lisa_support: Can we leave variant_pin=true until tomorrow morning PST to be extra safe?

acme_ops: That's fine. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

matt_cs: Closing the escalation once we confirm no new mixed-variant events within 24h. I'll schedule a postmortem entry and follow-up with a changelog note about affinity behavior in fallbacks.

lisa_support: Postmortem assigned to eng-runtime + eng-sre. Thanks team.
